samples.rationale: Clinical summary for direct care team coordination requires essential clinical, demographic, and current admission data to support patient treatment decisions and continuity of care within the hospital.

Clinical summary requires patient identification, diagnoses, medications, allergies, lab results, clinical encounters, and imaging reports to enable the care team to coordinate patient treatment safely and effectively.

A clinical summary is prepared for the care team to coordinate treatment of one patient. The selected fields provide essential clinical, demographic, and administrative information necessary to support this purpose while respecting data minimization principles.

Minimal necessary clinical, administrative, and demographic data to enable the care team to provide coordinated medical treatment, diagnose conditions, manage medications safely, and identify allergies. Direct identifiers pseudonymised to protect patient privacy while enabling clinical communication.
Clinical summary for care team provision of medical services; direct identifiers pseudonymised on export per regulatory requirement.

Ward staff require current patient lists with last encounter times for real-time care coordination and patient safety. This extraction provides only the direct identifiers and administrative status necessary for ongoing care operations.</anionale>
</invoke>
Care coordination requires knowing which patients are on each ward and when they were last clinically assessed to ensure appropriate continuity of care and clinical handoffs between teams.
Ward staff require current patient location and last clinical encounter timestamp to coordinate ongoing care and ensure continuity of treatment.
Extraction identifies current ward patients and their last clinical encounters to support daily care coordination and ward management decisions.
Patient identification, current ward location, and most recent clinical encounter time enable real-time care coordination and allow clinicians to assess timeliness of clinical evaluation.
Minimal clinical data extraction necessary to review medication appropriateness against current diagnosis and documented allergies for safe care coordination.

These fields are necessary to perform a comprehensive medication review against the patient's current diagnosis and documented allergies, which is essential for safe and coordinated care. The minimal set of fields ensures data minimisation while enabling the clinical review task.
Extraction of the patient's current medication, primary diagnosis, and documented allergies is necessary to perform care coordination and ensure medication safety through clinical review.

This extraction retrieves the patient's current medications, diagnoses, and known allergies to enable clinicians to review medication appropriateness and identify potential contraindications, supporting safe care coordination.

Extraction of the subject patient's medication, diagnosis and allergy records to enable clinical review of medication appropriateness. Only clinical and administrative fields necessary for medication safety reconciliation are extracted.

To send appointment reminders, this extraction provides patient contact details and appointment date necessary to fulfill the scheduling service patients consented to during registration. Data is retained for 30 days and then purged.
Contact details and appointment dates are essential to deliver appointment reminders as a core component of the patient registration and scheduling service to which patients consented.
Patient contact information and encounter dates are minimally necessary to send appointment reminders, fulfilling the registration and scheduling purpose for which patients provided their data.

Patient contact information (phone, email) and identification (MRN, name) are necessary to send personalized appointment reminders, while encounter_datetime specifies when the scheduled appointment occurs.

Appointment reminders are essential for the registration and scheduling purposes for which patients provided their data. The extraction includes only contact and appointment information necessary to deliver this reminder service.
Invoice reconciliation with payers requires invoice details, patient identification, and service encounter dates to verify the charges and settle accounts for services rendered.

Invoice reconciliation requires the patient's identifier, invoice details, and payer information to enable the accounts team to verify charges and complete settlement of amounts due for services provided.

Billing reconciliation requires invoice identification, billed amounts, payer details, and administrative service context. Clinical diagnosis data is not permitted under the billing settlement purpose policy.

Billing settlement requires invoice and payer details linked to service encounters to reconcile charges. Only administrative and financial data categories permitted by the purpose policy are extracted; clinical data including diagnosis is excluded as it falls outside permitted categories for this purpose.

Invoice and payer details are necessary to settle amounts due. Patient identifier and admission context enable matching services billed to the patient's encounter. Clinical data cannot be included as diagnosis is not a permitted category for billing settlement.</anionale>
</invoke>

Walk-in front-desk registration requires identification, contact, and demographic data. Insurance data is categorized as financial and falls outside the permitted categories for the patient registration purpose per binding policy constraints.

Front-desk walk-in patient registration and scheduling. Insurance data excluded as financial category is not permitted under patient_registration purpose; would require separate billing_settlement extraction if needed.

This extraction supports walk-in patient registration using only demographic and contact data within permitted categories. Insurance details are excluded as the financial category falls outside the purpose policy scope.

Front desk registration requires personal, contact, and administrative information for patient identification and scheduling. Financial data categories, including insurance details, are outside the permitted scope for this purpose.

Patient registration requires identification, contact details, and demographics for front-desk intake. Insurance policy data is excluded as financial information is not permitted for this purpose by the purpose policy.
Extraction of the patient's diagnosis, medications, allergies, and clinical encounter details is necessary to support ward round coordination and ensure safe, timely provision of medical care.
Extract patient's diagnosis, current medications, and allergies for ward round clinical decision-making. Retention limited to 90 days per purpose policy; secondary research use not permitted.

Extraction retrieves patient diagnosis and medication for ward round care coordination. Direct identifiers are pseudonymised on export; retention limited to 90 days with audit-logged deletion per policy.

Extract current diagnosis, medication, allergies, and clinical context for immediate ward round summary and care coordination. Direct identifiers are pseudonymised on export; retention limited to 90 days per purpose policy, ensuring compliance with India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023.

Ward round summaries require current diagnosis, medications, and admission context for clinical care coordination. The patient's direct identifier is pseudonymised for security. No secondary uses are permitted by the care coordination purpose policy.</anionale>
</invoke>
Extraction of current diagnosis and allergies for consultant care coordination under legitimate use basis. Data retained for 90 days per purpose policy to support ongoing medical treatment.

The consultant requires current diagnosis and allergy information to coordinate safe patient care. Retention is limited to the 90-day policy maximum; direct identifiers are pseudonymised on export per policy requirements.

Extract patient's current diagnosis and allergies for care coordination with consultant. Pseudonymised identifiers, encrypted transit and storage, and audit logging ensure DPDP Act compliance within the 90-day retention ceiling.

Extract patient's current diagnosis and allergies from EHR to support consultant-driven care coordination and clinical decision-making, with patient identifier pseudonymised on export per policy requirements.

Patient's current diagnosis and allergies are necessary for care coordination by the consultant. Direct identifiers will be pseudonymised on export per statutory requirement; retention limited to 90 days per purpose policy.</anionale>
</invoke>

This extraction supports reconciliation of the patient's outstanding invoice with the payer. Minimal data necessary for billing settlement is collected: patient identification, contact details, invoice data, and administrative context to identify the service delivery timeframe.</anionale>
</invoke>

Extract patient identification, contact, and invoice details to reconcile outstanding charges with payer. Data limited to administrative, financial, and contact categories necessary for billing settlement, with retention aligned to policy ceiling of 365 days.

Extraction retrieves financial, administrative, contact, and identification data needed to reconcile the patient's invoice with payer, adhering to the binding purpose policy which restricts billing settlement to these four data categories only.

Invoice reconciliation with the payer requires patient identification, admission context, encounter timing, and billing information within permitted administrative and financial categories. This extract enables settlement of amounts due for services provided while respecting data minimisation and binding purpose restrictions.

Extraction confined to direct identifiers, contact, and financial data necessary for invoice reconciliation under the binding policy for billing settlement. Clinical data (diagnosis, medication) cannot be included; clinical category is not within permitted categories for this purpose. Retention set to policy ceiling of 365 days.
Medication and allergy data is necessary and sufficient for safe clinical care coordination during ward rounds. Direct identifiers are pseudonymised on export per binding policy requirements.

Ward clinicians require current medication and allergy information to safely coordinate treatment, prevent adverse drug interactions, and make informed clinical decisions during rounds.</anionale>
</invoke>

Ward round medication and allergy summary requires only clinical and administrative data permitted by policy; direct identifiers will be pseudonymised on export via PSEUDO-EXPORT, and all data will be automatically purged within the 90-day retention ceiling. No onward uses are declared, consistent with the binding policy prohibition.

Current medications and allergies are essential clinical information required for safe patient care during ward rounds. Processing is limited to the minimal data necessary for this clinical care coordination purpose, with direct identifiers pseudonymised and retention limited to 90 days per policy.
Extract current medications and allergies (with encounter context) to enable safe clinical decision-making during the patient's ward round under the legitimate care coordination purpose.

Desk staff require patient registration and demographic details to verify the walk-in patient's identity and check for duplicate registrations to prevent fraudulent or duplicate entries in the system.
Desk staff require the patient's identity and contact details to verify walk-in registration information and confirm accuracy for proper scheduling and service provision.
Registration confirmation for walk-in patient with duplicate detection. Fields are limited to registration and demographic data necessary for enrollment and identity verification.

Desk staff requires registration and demographic data to confirm the walk-in patient's identity and establish their medical record. Scope limited to subject patient to ensure purpose limitation compliance; de-duplication is achieved through targeted matching of this patient's data against stored records, not blanket retrieval of all patient records.
Confirm walk-in patient registration details at desk and check all patient records for duplicates to ensure data quality and prevent erroneous duplicate registrations.

sampling: Claude Code headless (claude -p) on a subscription sign-in; our system prompt replaces Claude Code's; no tools, no MCP servers, no skills; run from an empty directory; effort high (pinned); no temperature or seed set
